newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Macraes dampens speculation on gold find.
newsitem.headline: Macraes dampens speculation on gold find.

text.p: Speculation that Macraes Mining has made a big West Coast gold find has been dampened by the company's managing director, Patrick O'Connor, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Tuesday.
O'Connor said Macraes had just finished drilling to a depth below the shaft of the old Blackwater Mine at Waiuta near Reefton.
It was too early to say what the results were and he put down the speculation to "local gossip".
The diamond drilling of the parent hole to a depth between 150 meters and 200m below the old Blackwater shaft of 800m had been completed.
A number of "daughter" holes would fan out from the parent hole, with the results of the tests from these intercepts expected to be completed by March.
Macraes planned expansion of its East Otago gold-mine would have spinoffs for the company and its local community, chairman Brettney Fogarty said in the interim report.
The new plant will involve construction of a stand-alone treatment plant capable of processing six million tonnes of ore a year.

Fogarty said that, together with the associated infrastructure, the new plant would cost about $120 million and would be separate from an existing plant which would continue to treat three million tonnes of ore a year.

"The new plant will create significant advantages for both the community and the company. Greater economies of scale, reducing risk to the company by having two process facilities yielding income, preferential ore treatment and increased flexibility in future mine planning will make Macraes a significant company in the gold industry."
When complete, the project would employ 500 people, including the company's employees and contract staff, Mr Fogarty said.
The expansion would yield between 320,000 ounces and 350,000 ounces of gold a year.
The operating costs were expected to be much lower than present "life of mine" costs.
The extent of such reductions would be further defined once the mining contract had been awarded.

"The company will immediately process the applications for resource consents and permits for the expanded project. The expected time for the granting of all resource consents and permits is between nine and 18 months. This is a condition precedent for the expansion to go ahead."
It was expected the plant would take 12 months to build once resource consents and permits were granted.

The company also intended increasing its exploration drilling programme at Macraes by 100 percent for at least three years. The gold project was expected to have seven drilling rigs working full-time during that period.
